It's time to face it, you are not what you once were.

The cycles wear on you. Combat maneuvers jar your creaking bones and your skin is tanned by the radiation of distant stars whose light grows dimmer in your eyes.

But the things you have seen! The works of dead empires, the fresh faces of green crew on their first op; tactical lasers glittering in the debris of forgotten battles.

You've lived a life beyond the imagination of the planet-bound. But it is a life hard-lived.

Your story could end here, starfarer. You can retire, enjoy yourself, and finally rest.

The question is, where and how?

It's time to face it, you are not what you once were.

The cycles wear on you. Combat maneuvers jar your creaking bones and your skin is tanned by the radiation of distant stars whose light grows dimmer in your eyes.

But the things you have seen! Death to wonder; the works of dead empires and fresh faces green crew on their first op; tactical lasers glittering in the debris of forgotten battles.

You've lived a life beyond the imagination of the planet-bound. But it is a life hard-lived.

Your story can end here, starfarer. It's time to enjoy your retirement.

The question is, where and how?

Gilead.

A garden world, a human world, the farthest thing from the death and cold of space. Surrounded by the blessing of life and living.

Tartessus.

You may finally rest, letting each day present you with a tapestry of sun-lit clouds over endless plains.

Qaras.

Where you may rest upon a throne atop the rabble and riot, a place you've earned by grit, blood, and lucre.

Chalcedon.

Your Path, you decide, leads into the eye of the storm. That is where peace may be found, if the divine so wills it.

Eochu Bres.

You envision a palace set upon the mountains in a raw, new land whose life and living is wrought by the ingenuity of humanity... and its creations.

It will be the ultimate celebration of the tool-makers, the world-shapers who claim the raw clay of the universe and produce splendor and wealth; it is all that it means to be human and more.

The Galatia Academy.

A ray of knowledge illuminating the shadows of war, a beacon of hope and education guiding those who are honest and true. Your influence may better the minds you nurture - one small part of lifting the Persean Sector out of this dark age.

Coatl Academy.

If humanity is to survive this long dark era, it needs to instill discipline, honor, and excellence in those fresh-faced cadets who will one day become officers in the Hegemony navy.

They stand against chaos and warlordism. They will defend the Persean Sector from inhuman threats both known and unknown. If the Domain is to be rebuilt, it will be by their blood.

You can do your part to help them do theirs.

Fikenhild.

An ocean of freedom and leisure - for those who, like you, can afford clear skies, endless seas, and a penthouse atop one of the five glittering arcologies.

Kazeron.

Heart of the Persean League and the rising power of the Sector. If there is to be a future for humanity, it may very well be forged here.

You are the executive officer of your colonial apparatus, majority-owner of most key infrastructure. But you aspire to be more than a bureaucrat: what if you were a leader?

Now you may dedicate yourself to this work, transforming the polity into something more than a legal entity enumerating a wage-roll of mercenaries, contractors, and desperate fortune-seekers.

Mass-fabricated shelters will become homes; the sprawl slumped along webs of maximum-efficiency grown outward from spaceports will become towns, communities.

Perhaps one day these shining cities and their inhabitants will share a sense of purpose and being: a true polity.

You are demarchon, leader of the people. More than a mere executive officer of a colonial apparatus, more than a distant majority-owner of key infrastructure and bureaucrat.

Now you may dedicate yourself to this work, transforming the polity into something more than a legal entity enumerating a wage-roll of mercenaries, contractors, and desperate fortune-seekers.

Mass-fabricated shelters will become homes; the sprawl slumped along webs of maximum-efficiency grown outward from spaceports will become towns, communities.

Perhaps one day these shining cities and their inhabitants will share a sense of purpose and being: a true polity.

Asharu, desert world.

Few would choose to make it their home, but you are someone quite unlike most.

Nova Maxios.

Where fate is self-made, and you are your accomplishments, not the name someone else gave you.
Finally, a time for rest.

You still hear the whispers of the moons, the songs of the stars. You live at such a velocity that it feels impossible to stop now.

There is no part of you that cannot be replaced; there are chems and replacements to enhance failing senses, overlaid and embedded smart-systems to assist failing memory and reaction time. Modules and modifications integrated into your body and mind. There are even dealers in lost miracles of the Domain - irreplaceable nanoscale devices, artificial machine-proteins, components only found in forgotten orbits of ruined worlds.

But they will become more and more expensive.

Your story could end here, starfarer. You can retire, enjoy yourself, and finall get some rest.

The question is, where and how?
